subject: FlowMart checkout: urgent fallback & product tradeoffs
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@flowmart.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@flowmart.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Latency spike + throughput drop impacting FlowMart checkout

Hi Mina,

We started seeing a big spike in p95 latency and an overall drop in throughput affecting our checkout-confirmation API at ~08:50 PDT. The spike correlates with a surge of simultaneous cart checks — user-visible timeouts are happening (~10% error rate on confirm). Attached is a short snippet of the runtime logs and our internal traces (flowmart_latency_log_1012.txt).

Can REDWOOD perform any immediate mitigation? Options we discussed on our side: route some traffic to a read-only fallback, or temporarily throttle heavy merchant accounts. We need to know if you can:
- enable a short-lived model fallback to a lower-cost variant (we accept a small quality delta for 1–2 hours), or
- apply a per-customer QPS cap from your side, or
- flip any KV-cache TTLs you control.

We’re on standby and can provide more traces. This is high impact for our Black Friday trial.

– Lucy Chen
Head of Engineering, FlowMart

Attachments: flowmart_latency_log_1012.txt

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@flowmart.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Latency spike + throughput drop impacting FlowMart checkout

Thanks Lucy — we see the spike in our internal telemetry as well (p95 up ~2.3x, throughput drop ~30% since 08:45). Karthik / Ben / Marissa — looping you in for immediate triage.

Immediate asks / constraints:
1) Customer prefers minimal manual steps — they explicitly consent to a temporary quality vs latency tradeoff for 60–120 minutes.
2) Any routing fallback should preserve request/response schema (no behavior changes besides score degradation).
3) We need a clear customer-facing blurb we can send within 30 minutes.

Suggested short-term mitigations to evaluate (please call out risk + ETA):
- Fast path: route FlowMart traffic to the dedicated-lowlat pool (if capacity exists) — Karthik, can you confirm capacity and warm instances?
- Fallback model: enable quantized / smaller variant for FlowMart traffic only (Ben) — what's expected quality delta and how fast can we switch?
- QPS cap: per-customer throttle to smooth the burst (Karthik) — are there ripple effects on autoscaler?
- Cache tweaks: reduce KV cache TTL or warm prefix cache (Ben / infra) — safe to change live?

Deliverables / timeline: 15m triage update, 45m mitigation plan, send initial customer note once mitigation is in progress.

I’ve attached a quick internal rollout plan (MAP_rollout_plan_v2.pdf) with a canary path.

– Mina
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability

Attachments: MAP_rollout_plan_v2.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@flowmart.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:39:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Latency spike + throughput drop impacting FlowMart checkout

On 10/12/26 09:13, Lucy Chen wrote:
> We started seeing a big spike in p95 latency...

Quick triage notes:
- Root symptom looks like KV-cache evaporation on the gen-api path for FlowMart (hot prefixes) + a burst that caused contention in the attention kernels on several hosts.
- Autoscaler did not immediately spin up because request patterns were bursty and instances hit scheduling backlog.

Immediate mitigation I can apply now (ETA 12–20m):
1) Temporarily enforce per-customer soft-QPS cap at the ingress for FlowMart (throttle to 60% of peak) — low risk, immediate.
2) Route 20% of FlowMart traffic to the dedicated-lowlat pool (if approved) — I need the green light, will take ~18m to provision routing and warm.
3) Disable aggressive KV eviction for the FlowMart shard (reduce eviction aggressiveness) — will increase memory footprint but should reduce p95; ETA 10m.

Risk notes: routing to dedicated pool will use reserved capacity; if sustained it may bump other customers on that pool. Fallback to smaller model will likely reduce answer fidelity — product should sign off.

Runbook referenced: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-eviction-and-routing (internal link)

I’ll start with the soft-QPS cap + eviction tweak and report back.

– Karthik
Staff SRE

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@flowmart.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Latency spike + throughput drop impacting FlowMart checkout

On Tue, Oct 12, 2026 at 09:39 Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick triage notes...

Implemented changes I can push now (canary first):
- Reduced micro-batching window from 12ms -> 6ms for the gen-api consumer for FlowMart origin (tradeoff: slightly higher per-token compute, but reduces batching-induced queue spike).
- Applied a conservative quantized fallback profile that is compatible with the request schema. Quality delta estimated at ~3–4% on our internal checkout prompts.

Can deploy these to a 10% canary in ~14m and bump to 50% in another 20m if metrics look stable. I attached a brief canary snapshot for metrics (canary_metrics_snapshot.png).

If product approves the fallback profile, we can expedite to 50% after the first canary window.

– Ben
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachments: canary_metrics_snapshot.png

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@flowmart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike + throughput drop impacting FlowMart checkout — customer note

Lucy — updating you with actions taken and next steps so you can share with your team:

What we did (10:10–10:20 PDT):
- Enforced a short soft-QPS cap for FlowMart ingress to smooth the burst.
- Reduced KV eviction aggressiveness for FlowMart shard to keep hot prefixes warm.
- Deployed a 10% canary of a conservative quantized fallback and reduced micro-batching for FlowMart traffic.

Expected user impact:
- p95 should begin to improve within the next 5–15 minutes; throughput may remain below peak until autoscaler warms additional instances.
- Response quality: very small degradation (~3–4%) on some checkout prompts while the fallback path is routed.

What we need from FlowMart:
- Confirm you accept the temporary quality tradeoff for the next 60–120 minutes.
- Please share any real-user examples where quality is unacceptable so we can roll back those routes.

Next steps (internal):
- 10:40 PDT: evaluate canary metrics; if healthy, expand to 50% and continue warming dedicated pool (Karthik / Ben).
- Postmortem: we’ll open SUP-4521 and share a draft by EOD 10/14.

Customer-facing note you can copy:
"We’re actively applying a temporary routing and fallback plan to reduce latency visible on checkout. You may see a small quality difference while the fallback is active. We expect improvement within 30 minutes and will follow up with a postmortem."

Lucy — please let me know and I’ll mark the canary expansion on your approval.

– Mina
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
